summary.text: An 88-year-old woman with hypertension, diabetes mellitus, hypothyroidism and a history of gastrectomy for gastric cancer presented with a two-week history of refractory leg edema while taking azosemide, antihypertensive agents and levothyroxine.

Examination showed a grade 3/6 systolic murmur and bilateral pitting edema; laboratory tests showed anemia and hypoalbuminemia. ECG showed normal sinus rhythm with an LV strain pattern and chest radiography showed cardiomegaly. Echocardiography showed hyperdynamic LV wall motion, EF 80%, LV hypertrophy, a calcified aortic valve, pericardial effusion, peak aortic jet velocity 4.5 m/s and mean gradient 46 mmHg, consistent with severe AS.

Thiamine deficiency was suspected; intravenous fursultiamine was given empirically after blood sampling, followed by oral replacement (75 mg/day). The pretreatment thiamine level of 15 ng/mL confirmed the diagnosis.

At one month the thiamine level was 28 ng/mL and edema had improved. At eight months thiamine was 173 ng/mL with EF 50%, E/A 0.9, LVOT-VTI 13.1 cm and peak aortic jet velocity 3.3 m/s; pericardial effusion was reduced but mild, and AS was reassessed as moderate.
She remained clinically stable under conservative management with continued thiamine replacement over 14 months of follow-up. Natriuretic peptides and right heart catheterization were not obtained.

summary.text: An 89-year-old woman with liver cirrhosis on long-term diuretic therapy and hypothyroidism, without gastrointestinal surgery history, presented with an eight-week history of refractory leg edema and a three-week non-healing right lower leg ulcer following a skin injury. Medications included azosemide, furosemide, spironolactone, branched-chain amino acids and levothyroxine.

Examination showed a grade 3/6 systolic murmur and bilateral pitting edema; laboratory tests showed anemia and hypoalbuminemia. ECG showed normal sinus rhythm and chest radiography a cardiothoracic ratio of 52%. Echocardiography showed hyperdynamic LV wall motion, EF 74% without LV hypertrophy, a calcified aortic valve, peak aortic jet velocity 3.3 m/s and mean gradient 20 mmHg, consistent with moderate AS.
Thiamine deficiency was suspected and oral fursultiamine (75 mg/day) was started empirically after blood sampling; a low pretreatment thiamine level of 20 ng/mL supported the diagnosis.

Edema and ulcer partially improved within one month and resolved completely after three months with a thiamine level of 237 ng/mL. Follow-up echocardiography showed EF 68%, E/A 0.7, LVOT-VTI 19.7 cm and peak aortic jet velocity 2.2 m/s; AS was reassessed as mild.
She remained clinically stable under conservative management with continued thiamine replacement over six months of follow-up. Natriuretic peptides and right heart catheterization were not obtained.
